To add file upload support for an `Article` model using Rails' ActiveStorage and allow a single attached image called `cover_image`, you need to perform a few steps. First, ensure that your database migration is set up correctly. Run the following command to generate a migration that adds an attachment column to your `articles` table: ```bash rails generate migration AddCoverImageToArticles cover_image:attachment ``` Then, apply the migration by running: ```bash rails db:migrate ``` Next, update your `Article` model to include the ActiveStorage functionality for attachments. Modify the `app/models/article.rb` file as follows: ```ruby class Article < ApplicationRecord has_one_attached :cover_image end ``` With these changes in place, you can now attach a single image to an instance of the `Article` model using ActiveStorage. Here's how you might update an existing article or create a new one with a cover image: ```ruby # Create a new article with a cover image article = Article.new(title: "My First Article") file_path = Rails.root.join('public', 'images', 'my_image.jpg') article.cover_image.attach(io: File.open(file_path), filename: 'my_image.jpg') article.save! # Update an existing article with a new cover image existing_article = Article.find(1) new_file_path = Rails.root.join('public', 'images', 'new_image.jpg') existing_article.cover_image.attach(io: File.open(new_file_path), filename: 'new_image.jpg') existing_article.save! ``` In the views, you can display the attached image using helpers provided by ActiveStorage. For example, in a form to update an article: ```erb <%= form_with model: @article do |form| %> <%= form.file_field :cover_image %> <%= form.submit "Save" %> <% end %> <% if @article.cover_image.attached? %> <%= image_tag @article.cover_image, alt: @article.title %> <% else %>

No cover image available

<% end %> ``` These steps will add file upload support to your `Article` model using Rails' ActiveStorage, allowing a single attached image called `cover_image`.
